parsed.justification: The replication re-ran the core computational pipeline (NCBI genome set selection, Prokka+Roary pan-genome calling, and openness assessment) and reproduced the qualitative conclusion of an open pan-genome with continued gene discovery. Quantitatively, category counts differ (notably core +8.5% and soft-core -20.3%), but core+soft-core is close (+2.1%) and shell/cloud/total are within a few percent, consistent with dataset drift (124 vs 127 genomes) and minor version/parameter differences. The probiotic marker gene claim could not be evaluated due to blocked supplementary data, limiting full claim coverage.

parsed.justification: The replication reproduces the main pan-genome conclusions despite a small cohort mismatch likely due to database curation drift (124 vs 127 genomes) and minor tool-version changes. Total pan-genome size, shell/cloud counts, combined core+soft-core size, and the key qualitative claim of an open pan-genome all agree closely, although the split between core and soft-core differs more noticeably. One important paper claim was not checked: the ~70% probiotic marker genes being in the core/soft-core genome, so this is not a full replication.

Minor discrepancies in core/soft-core counts are reasonably attributed to justifiable differences in the input dataset and software versions. The verdict is 'PARTIAL' as a secondary analysis of probiotic marker genes was blocked by inaccessible supplementary data, preventing a complete replication of all claims.
